<|det|>title [68, 255, 178, 273]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [66, 294, 930, 329]<|/det|>The DownloadChunks() function will panic with a nil pointer dereference if grpc.NewClient() fails, as the deferred cleanup function attempts to call Close() on a nil connection object. <|det|>text [73, 337, 530, 351]<|/det|>api/clients/v2/validator/grpc_manager.go:DownloadChunks() <|det|>text [73, 354, 731, 852]<|/det|>func (m *validatorGRPCManager) DownloadChunks( ctx context.Context, key v3.0.Key, operatorID core.OperatorID, ) (*grpcNode.GetChunksReply, error) { // TODO(code.little) we can get a tighter bound? maxIoObject = 16 * units.MiB // maximum size of the original blob encodingRate = 8 // worst case scenario if one validator has 100% stake fudgeObject := units.MiB // to allow for some overhead from things like protobuf encoding maxMessageSize := maxIoObjectEncodingRate + fudgeFactor socket, ok := m.socketMap[operatorID] if lok { return nil, fmt.Error("Operator %s not found in socket map", operatorID.Hex()) } conn, err := grpc.NewClient( socket.GetOutputStream(socket); grpc.WithTransportCredentials(success, NewCredentials(), grpc.WithInfoFullCallOptions[grpc.MaxCallRecvMsgSize(maxMessageSize)], ) ) defer func[] { err := conn.Close() // @Audit conn is nil if grpc.NewClient failed if err != nil { m.logger.Error("validator retriever failed to close connection", "err", err) } } if err != nil { return nil, fit.Error("failed to create connection to operator %s: %w", operatorId.Hex(), err) } client := grpcnode.NewRetrievalClient(conn) request := &grpcnode.GetChunksRequest{ BlobKey: key[1], } reply, err := client.GetChunks(Ctx, request) if err != nil { return nil, fit.Error("failed to get chunks from operator %s: %w", operatorId.Hex(), err) } return reply, nil } <|det|>text [66, 864, 931, 898]<|/det|>When grpc.NewClient() returns an error, conn will be nil. The code then enters the early return path, but the deferred function still executes and attempts to call conn.Close(), causing a panic. <|det|>footer [75, 924, 206, 945]<|/det|>signal prime <|det|>page_number [810, 931, 881, 946]<|/det|>Page | 13

<|det|>header [751, 60, 882, 74]<|/det|>Detailed Findings
<|det|>title [68, 104, 238, 119]<|/det|>Recommendations
<|det|>text [66, 143, 930, 172]<|/det|>Move the deferred cleanup function to run after the error check. This ensures the cleanup only happens when a valid connection exists. The fix is simple and prevents the nil pointer crash.
<|det|>title [68, 206, 169, 221]<|/det|>Resolution
<|det|>text [66, 245, 930, 274]<|/det|>The issue has been resolved by relocating the deferred connection cleanup to occur only after confirming that the connection was successfully established. The resolution can be found in the PR #2131.
